Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

# the aggregate signature on its root statement so the pair travels as one
# object across implementations. The integer, frame and signature

# the nested bundles keep their existing encode_hbpb bytes. Decoding

# to check_hp, which remains the sole verifier.

HPB_WIRE_TAG = b"ts/hpb/v1"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HPB:
    """A compact multi-bundle membership proof with its root signature.

    The fields, in order, are ``proof`` (an :class:`HP`) and
    ``signature`` (the :class:`AggregateSignature` on the proof's
    ``b"hp/r" || U64(total) || root`` statement, the exact message
    :func:`make_hp` returns). The dataclass is frozen, positionally
    constructible and compared by value, and carries no network, storage
    or hidden state. Field types and bounds are not checked at
    construction time — :func:`encode_hpb` checks the structure and
    :func:`verify_hpb` is the way to test a bundle afterwards.

    proof: HP
    signature: AggregateSignature


def encode_hp(proof: HP) -> bytes:
    """Canonically encode an HP membership proof for transport or persistence.

    ``b"ts/hp/v1"``, ``VARINT(total)``, the index count as a 4-byte

    the proof's strictly increasing order, the bundle count as a 4-byte
    unsigned big-endian integer, one frame per bundle — the 4-byte
    unsigned big-endian length ``len(E)`` followed by the raw bytes
    ``E = encode_hbpb(bundle_value)`` (never empty) — and the sibling
    count as a 4-byte unsigned big-endian integer followed by the raw
    32-byte sibling digests in their original leaf-to-root, left-to-right

    followed by the shortest unsigned big-endian value (zero is the
    single byte ``00``, positive values carry no leading zero). The
    integer and frame conventions are exactly those of the existing HBPB
    transport bundle. The indices must be non-empty, strictly increasing,
    unique and within ``0 <= i < total``, the bundle count must equal the
    index count, and the sibling count must be the unique one derived
    from ``total`` and the indices by the compact multi-proof walk.

    argument or wrong field types raise TypeError and illegal bounds, an
    empty index tuple, a bundle tuple that does not pair one-to-one with
    the indices, a sibling that is not exactly 32 bytes, a sibling count
    other than the one ``total`` and the indices determine, a
    structurally illegal nested bundle or an over-long frame raises
    ValueError — but the bundles are not verified: :func:`check_hp`
    (through :func:`verify_hpb`) stays the way to verify a proof
    afterwards. The output for a given proof is unique and the encoding
    carries no network, storage or hidden state.
    """
    indices, total, bundles, siblings = _validate_hp_structure(proof)
    try:
        if len(bundles) != len(indices):
            raise ValueError(
                "proof.bundles must pair one-to-one with proof.indices"
            )
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError("too many HBPB archive proof bundles") from None
    required_siblings = _required_history_multi_proof_siblings(
        total, indices
    )
    if len(siblings) != required_siblings:
        raise ValueError(
            "proof.siblings count is not the one determined by total "
            "and indices"
        )
    if len(indices) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("too many indices")
    if len(siblings) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("too many siblings")

    encoded_bundles = []
    for position, bundle in enumerate(bundles):
        encoded_bundle = encode_hbpb(bundle)
        if len(encoded_bundle) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
            raise ValueError(
                f"hp bundle {position + 1} encoding too long"
            )

    buffer += _encode_varint(total)
    buffer += len(indices).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)

        buffer += _encode_varint(index)
    buffer += len(encoded_bundles).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
    for encoded_bundle in encoded_bundles:
        buffer += len(encoded_bundle).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
        buffer += encoded_bundle
    buffer += len(siblings).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)

    return bytes(buffer)

    length followed by its shortest unsigned big-endian value, zero
    encoded as the single byte ``00``), the 4-byte non-zero index count
    followed by one canonical ``VARINT`` per strictly increasing index,
    the 4-byte bundle count (which must equal the index count) followed
    by that many non-empty bundle frames (a 4-byte non-zero length
    followed by bytes that :func:`decode_hbpb` accepts), and the 4-byte
    sibling count followed by exactly that many raw 32-byte sibling
    digests, where the count must be the unique one derived from
    ``total`` and the disclosed indices. A non-bytes argument raises
    TypeError; a wrong or missing tag, an empty index list, a
    non-positive or over-64-bit ``total``, an index outside
    ``0 <= i < total``, indices that are not strictly increasing and
    unique, a bundle count that does not match the index count, an empty,
    truncated or non-canonical bundle frame, a missing or extra sibling
    relative to the count ``total`` and the indices require, a sibling
    that is not exactly 32 bytes, a non-canonical integer (leading zero
    or over-long length), truncation, or trailing bytes raises
    ValueError. A successfully decoded proof re-encodes to exactly the
    input bytes.

    Decoding only restores the structure: each nested bundle is decoded
    with :func:`decode_hbpb` (which verifies no bundle and checks no
    signature). A structurally legal proof whose nested bundles do not
    verify is returned normally, and :func:`check_hp` (through
    :func:`verify_hpb`) reports it as ``False``.
    """

        raise TypeError("blob must be bytes")

        raise ValueError("bad HP proof tag")

    total, offset = _read_varint(blob, offset, what="HP proof total")
    if total <= 0:
        raise ValueError("HP proof total must be positive")
    if total > 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF:
        raise ValueError("HP proof total too large")

        raise ValueError("truncated HP proof index count")
    index_count = int.from_bytes(blob[offset:offset + 4], "big")
    offset += 4
    if index_count == 0:
        raise ValueError("HP proof indices must be non-empty")
    indices = []
    for _ in range(index_count):
        index, offset = _read_varint(blob, offset, what="HP proof index")
        indices.append(index)

    if offset + 4 > len(blob):
        raise ValueError("truncated HP proof bundle count")
    bundle_count = int.from_bytes(blob[offset:offset + 4], "big")
    offset += 4
    if bundle_count != index_count:
        raise ValueError(
            "HP proof bundle count must match the index count"
        )
    bundles = []
    for position in range(bundle_count):
        encoded_bundle, offset = _read_archive_block(
            blob,
            offset,
            what=f"HP proof bundle {position + 1}",
        )
        bundles.append(decode_hbpb(encoded_bundle))

    if offset + 4 > len(blob):
        raise ValueError("truncated HP proof sibling count")

    offset += 4
    required_siblings = _required_history_multi_proof_siblings(
        total, tuple(indices)
    )
    if sibling_count != required_siblings:
        raise ValueError(
            "HP proof sibling count is not the one determined by total "
            "and indices"
        )
    siblings = []
    for _ in range(sibling_count):
        if offset + HP_DIGEST_SIZE > len(blob):
            raise ValueError("truncated HP proof sibling")

            bytes(blob[offset:offset + HP_DIGEST_SIZE])

        offset += HP_DIGEST_SIZE

        raise ValueError("trailing bytes after HP proof")

        indices=tuple(indices),
        total=total,
        bundles=tuple(bundles),
        siblings=tuple(siblings),

        raise ValueError("non-canonical HP proof encoding")

def encode_hpb(bundle: HPB) -> bytes:

    The encoding is the direct concatenation, in order, of the tag
    ``b"ts/hpb/v1"``, the 4-byte unsigned big-endian length ``len(P)``
    followed by ``P = encode_hp(bundle.proof)`` (never empty), and then
    the signature frame: ``VARINT(R)``, ``VARINT(z)``, the 4-byte
    unsigned big-endian signer count and one ``VARINT(id)`` per ascending
    signer id. A ``VARINT`` is a 4-byte unsigned big-endian body length
    followed by the shortest unsigned big-endian value (zero is the
    single byte ``00``, positive values carry no leading zero); ``R``
    must be positive and ``z`` may be zero. The integer, frame and
    signature conventions are exactly those of the existing HBPB
    transport bundle.

    non-:class:`HP` proof argument, or wrong proof/signature field types,
    raise TypeError and illegal proof structure (the exact bounds of
    :func:`encode_hp`), a structurally illegal signature (a non-positive
    ``R``, a negative ``z``, an empty or non-strictly-increasing signer
    id tuple) or an over-long frame raises ValueError — but the proof is
    not verified and the signature is not checked against the root:
    :func:`verify_hpb` stays the way to verify a bundle afterwards. The
    output for a given bundle is unique and the encoding carries no
    network, storage or hidden state.

    if not isinstance(bundle, HPB):
        raise TypeError("bundle must be an HPB instance")

    signer_count = _check_history_proof_bundle_signature(bundle.signature)

        raise ValueError("hp proof encoding too long")

        raise ValueError("too many signer ids")

    buffer += len(encoded_proof).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
    buffer += encoded_proof
    buffer += _encode_varint(bundle.signature.R)
    buffer += _encode_varint(bundle.signature.z)
    buffer += signer_count.to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
    for signer_id in bundle.signature.signer_ids:
        buffer += _encode_varint(signer_id)
    return bytes(buffer)


def decode_hpb(blob: bytes) -> HPB:
    """Decode the canonical encoding produced by :func:`encode_hpb`.

    :func:`decode_hp` accepts, and then the signature frame: the
    length-prefixed integers ``R`` and ``z`` with ``R`` positive, the
    4-byte non-zero signer count and exactly that many strictly
    increasing positive signer ids. A non-bytes argument raises
    TypeError; a wrong or missing tag, a zero or over-long proof frame
    length, a non-canonical nested proof, a zero ``R``, a non-canonical
    integer (leading zero or over-long length), a zero signer count, a
    non-positive or non-increasing signer id, truncation, or trailing
    bytes raises ValueError. A successfully decoded bundle re-encodes to
    exactly the input bytes.

    with :func:`decode_hp` (which verifies no bundle and checks no
    signature) and the root signature is not checked. A structurally
    legal bundle whose nested bundles do not verify or whose signature
    does not sign the root is returned normally, and :func:`verify_hpb`
    reports it as ``False``.

        raise TypeError("blob must be bytes")

        raise ValueError("bad HPB tag")

    encoded_proof, offset = _read_archive_block(
        blob, offset, what="HPB proof"
    )
    proof = decode_hp(encoded_proof)

    signature, offset = _read_bundle_signature_frame(
        blob, offset, what="HPB"
    )
    if offset != len(blob):
        raise ValueError("trailing bytes after HPB")

    bundle = HPB(proof=proof, signature=signature)
    if encode_hpb(bundle) != blob:
        raise ValueError("non-canonical HPB encoding")

def verify_hpb(bundle: HPB, key: SigningDKGResult) -> bool:

    ``check_hp(bundle.proof, bundle.signature, key)``: the Merkle root

    :func:`verify_hbpb` against ``key`` and the signature verified on

    ``b"hp/r" || U64(total) || root``. Returns ``True`` only when all
    of them hold; a well-formed bundle with a tampered bundle, index,
    sibling or signature, a bundle swapped or altered, a missing or extra
    sibling, or one presented under another key, returns ``False``.

    A non-:class:`HPB` argument raises TypeError; illegal nested proof,
    bundle, signature or key structure raises TypeError/ValueError,
    exactly as :func:`check_hp` does.
    """

429	    length, a non-canonical nested proof, a zero ``R``, a non-canonical
430	    integer (leading zero or over-long length), a zero signer count, a
431	    non-positive or non-increasing signer id, truncation, or trailing
432	    bytes raises ValueError. A successfully decoded bundle re-encodes to
433	    exactly the input bytes.
434	
435	    Decoding only restores the structure: the nested proof is decoded
436	    with :func:`decode_hp` (which verifies no bundle and checks no
437	    signature) and the root signature is not checked. A structurally
438	    legal bundle whose nested bundles do not verify or whose signature
439	    does not sign the root is returned normally, and :func:`verify_hpb`
440	    reports it as ``False``.
441	    """
442	    if not isinstance(blob, bytes):
443	        raise TypeError("blob must be bytes")
444	    if not blob.startswith(HPB_WIRE_TAG):
445	        raise ValueError("bad HPB tag")
446	    offset = len(HPB_WIRE_TAG)
447	
448	    encoded_proof, offset = _read_archive_block(
449	        blob, offset, what="HPB proof"
450	    )
451	    proof = decode_hp(encoded_proof)
452	
453	    signature, offset = _read_bundle_signature_frame(
454	        blob, offset, what="HPB"
455	    )
456	    if offset != len(blob):
457	        raise ValueError("trailing bytes after HPB")
458	
459	    bundle = HPB(proof=proof, signature=signature)
460	    if encode_hpb(bundle) != blob:
461	        raise ValueError("non-canonical HPB encoding")
462	    return bundle

465	def verify_hpb(bundle: HPB, key: SigningDKGResult) -> bool:

469	    ``check_hp(bundle.proof, bundle.signature, key)``: the Merkle root
470	    is rebuilt from the proof, every disclosed bundle is re-checked with
471	    :func:`verify_hbpb` against ``key`` and the signature verified on
472	    the exact statement :func:`make_hp` returns,
473	    ``b"hp/r" || U64(total) || root``. Returns ``True`` only when all
474	    of them hold; a well-formed bundle with a tampered bundle, index,
475	    sibling or signature, a bundle swapped or altered, a missing or extra
476	    sibling, or one presented under another key, returns ``False``.

479	    bundle, signature or key structure raises TypeError/ValueError,
480	    exactly as :func:`check_hp` does.
481	    """

483	        raise TypeError("bundle must be an HPB instance")

487	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
488	# Canonical HPB archive: several whole HPB membership-proof transport
489	# bundles kept in their original order as one non-empty tuple, with one
490	# aggregate threshold-Schnorr signature authenticating both the bytes and
491	# their order over the archive's canonical framing. Mirrors the existing
492	# HBPB archive layer one level down: the value is frozen and stateless, the
493	# message can be taken through the two-round threshold signing flow as is,
494	# and decoding restores structure only — every nested bundle goes through
495	# decode_hpb, no bundle or signature is checked and no state is kept, so
496	# verify_hpba remains the sole verifier afterwards.
497	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
498	
499	HPBA_MESSAGE_TAG = b"ts/hpba/m1"
500	HPBA_WIRE_TAG = b"ts/hpba/w1"
501	
502	
503	@dataclass(frozen=True)
504	class HPBArchive:
505	    """A non-empty ordered archive of HPB bundles with one outer signature.
506	
507	    The fields, in order, are ``items`` — a non-empty tuple of
508	    :class:`HPB` values in archive order — and ``signature`` — the
509	    threshold Schnorr :class:`AggregateSignature` on
510	    :func:`hpba_message` of the items and the verifying public key.
511	    The dataclass is frozen, positionally constructible and compared by
512	    value; neither field has a default, the items keep their order and
513	    the archive carries no network, storage or hidden state. Neither
514	    field is checked at construction time — :func:`hpba_message`
515	    requires structurally legal items and :func:`verify_hpba` is the
516	    way to test an archive against a key afterwards.
517	    """
518	
519	    items: tuple[HPB, ...]
520	    signature: AggregateSignature
521	
522	
523	def hpba_message(
524	    items: tuple[HPB, ...], public_key: int
525	) -> bytes:
526	    """Encode the canonical message the threshold key signs for an archive.
527	
528	    The message is, in order, the tag ``b"ts/hpba/m1"``, the 32-byte
529	    ``SHA256`` digest of the canonical framing ``C`` and
530	    ``V(public_key)`` — a 4-byte unsigned big-endian length followed by
531	    the shortest unsigned big-endian value (zero is the single byte
532	    ``00``, positive values carry no leading zero). With
533	    ``E_i = encode_hpb(items[i])`` and ``n`` the item count, ``C`` is
534	    built in tuple order as ``U32(n) || Σ(U32(len(E_i)) || E_i)``;
535	    every ``U32`` is a 4-byte unsigned big-endian integer, the frames
536	    carry no separators and ``E_i`` is the existing canonical transport
537	    encoding of the bundle. The message carries no signature and keeps
538	    no state, and can be taken through the two-round threshold signing
539	    flow as is.
540	
541	    ``items`` must be a non-empty tuple of structurally legal
542	    :class:`HPB` values exactly as :func:`encode_hpb` requires and
543	    ``public_key`` a non-boolean non-negative integer. Wrong field or
544	    nested field types raise TypeError — a non-tuple items sequence, an
545	    item that is not an :class:`HPB`, or a non-integer (including
546	    boolean) public key; an empty items tuple, an illegal nested
547	    bundle, a negative public key or an over-long encoding raises
548	    ValueError.
549	    """
550	    if not isinstance(items, tuple):
551	        raise TypeError("items must be a tuple")
552	    for item in items:
553	        if not isinstance(item, HPB):
554	            raise TypeError("each archive item must be an HPB instance")
555	    if not isinstance(public_key, int) or isinstance(public_key, bool):
556	        raise TypeError("public_key must be an integer")
557	
558	    try:
559	        item_count = len(items)
560	    except OverflowError:
561	        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items") from None
562	    if item_count == 0:
563	        raise ValueError("archive items must be a non-empty tuple")
564	    if item_count > 0xFFFFFFFF:
565	        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items")
566	    if public_key < 0:
567	        raise ValueError("public_key must be non-negative")
568	
569	    # Encode every bundle first — each call raises TypeError/ValueError
570	    # for an illegal bundle exactly as the bundle codec does — and only
571	    # then frame the results, so a single illegal item aborts the whole
572	    # message.
573	    frames = []
574	    for index, item in enumerate(items):
575	        encoded = encode_hpb(item)
576	        if len(encoded) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
577	            raise ValueError(
578	                f"HPB archive item {index + 1} encoding too long"
579	            )
580	        frames.append(encoded)
581	
582	    framing = bytearray(item_count.to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False))
583	    for encoded in frames:
584	        framing += len(encoded).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
585	        framing += encoded
586	    return (
587	        HPBA_MESSAGE_TAG
588	        + hashlib.sha256(bytes(framing)).digest()
589	        + _encode_varint(public_key)
590	    )
591

593	def verify_hpba(
594	    archive: HPBArchive, key: SigningDKGResult
595	) -> bool:
596	    """Verify an archive of HPB bundles against the threshold key.
597	
598	    ``archive`` must be a structurally legal :class:`HPBArchive` and
599	    ``key`` a legal :class:`SigningDKGResult`. The outer signature and
600	    the key structure are checked first, as is the structure of every
601	    item, so an illegal outer signature or key is never masked by a bad
602	    nested bundle: a non-:class:`HPBArchive` argument, a non-tuple
603	    ``items`` field, a non-:class:`HPB` element or a
604	    non-:class:`SigningDKGResult` ``key`` raises TypeError, and an
605	    empty items tuple, an illegal outer signature structure, an illegal
606	    key structure or any structurally illegal nested bundle raises
607	    ValueError.
608	
609	    Every bundle is then passed to :func:`verify_hpb` in archive
610	    order, so each disclosed HP membership proof, the HBPB bundles it
611	    carries and its root signature must verify under ``key``; the
612	    canonical :func:`hpba_message` of the items and
613	    ``key.public_key`` is finally checked as the outer signature's
614	    threshold Schnorr message via :func:`verify_signature` with the
615	    key's group parameters. Returns ``True`` only when every
616	    per-bundle check and the outer signature check pass; a structurally
617	    legal archive whose nested bundle or outer signature does not match
618	    — including deleting, inserting, reordering or substituting a
619	    bundle, tampering with the outer signature, or presenting the
620	    archive under another key — returns ``False`` rather than raising.
621	    The function is stateless.
622	    """
623	    if not isinstance(archive, HPBArchive):
624	        raise TypeError(
625	            "archive must be an HPBArchive instance"
626	        )
627	    items = archive.items
628	    if not isinstance(items, tuple):
629	        raise TypeError("items must be a tuple")
630	    for item in items:
631	        if not isinstance(item, HPB):
632	            raise TypeError("each archive item must be an HPB instance")
633	    # Check the outer signature and the key before any nested bundle is
634	    # examined, so a bad bundle can never mask an illegal outer
635	    # signature or key; structurally validate every nested bundle too,
636	    # exactly as the single-bundle verifier validates its proof.
637	    _check_history_proof_bundle_signature(archive.signature)
638	    _result, public_key, field_prime, group_prime, generator = _check_signing_setup(key)
639	    _check_signing_dkg_structure(key)
640	    try:
641	        item_count = len(items)
642	    except OverflowError:
643	        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items") from None
644	    if item_count == 0:
645	        raise ValueError("archive items must be a non-empty tuple")
646	    for item in items:
647	        encode_hpb(item)
648	
649	    if not all(verify_hpb(item, key) for item in items):
650	        return False
651	    message = hpba_message(items, public_key)
652	    return verify_signature(
653	        message,
654	        archive.signature,
655	        public_key,
656	        group_prime=group_prime,
657	        generator=generator,
658	        prime=field_prime,
659	    )
660

662	def encode_hpba(archive: HPBArchive) -> bytes:
663	    """Canonically encode a non-empty ordered archive of HPB bundles as
664	    one self-delimiting object for transport or persistence.
665	
666	    The encoding is, in order, the tag ``b"ts/hpba/w1"``, the 4-byte
667	    unsigned big-endian item count (never zero), then one frame per
668	    bundle in tuple order — each the 4-byte unsigned big-endian byte
669	    length (never zero) followed by the exact bytes of
670	    :func:`encode_hpb` for that item, with no further separators —
671	    and finally the outer signature frame an :class:`AuditProofBundle`
672	    carries: ``VARINT(R)``, ``VARINT(z)``, the 4-byte unsigned
673	    big-endian signer count ``k`` and one ``VARINT(id)`` per ascending
674	    signer id. Every U32 is a 4-byte unsigned big-endian integer; a
675	    ``VARINT`` is a 4-byte unsigned big-endian body length followed by
676	    the shortest unsigned big-endian value (zero is the single byte
677	    ``00``, positive values carry no leading zero); ``R`` must be
678	    positive, ``z`` may be zero and the signer ids are a non-empty
679	    strictly increasing tuple of positive integers.
680	
681	    Only the archive container, each individual bundle and the outer
682	    signature are checked structurally — the items are not sorted or
683	    otherwise reordered, the outer signature is not matched against the
684	    bundles, no inner or outer signature is checked and no state is
685	    read: :func:`verify_hpba` stays the way to test an archive
686	    against a key afterwards. A non-:class:`HPBArchive` argument, a
687	    non-tuple ``items`` field or a non-:class:`HPB` element raises
688	    TypeError, as do wrong field types nested inside a bundle and a
689	    non-:class:`AggregateSignature` outer signature or one with wrong
690	    field types. An empty items tuple, an over-long count or frame,
691	    any structural error a bundle would raise on its own, or an
692	    illegal outer signature structure raises ValueError. The output
693	    for a given archive is unique and the encoding carries no
694	    network, storage or hidden state.
695	    """
696	    if not isinstance(archive, HPBArchive):
697	        raise TypeError(
698	            "archive must be an HPBArchive instance"
699	        )
700	    items = archive.items
701	    if not isinstance(items, tuple):
702	        raise TypeError("items must be a tuple")
703	    for item in items:
704	        if not isinstance(item, HPB):
705	            raise TypeError("each archive item must be an HPB instance")
706	    try:
707	        item_count = len(items)
708	    except OverflowError:
709	        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items") from None
710	    if item_count == 0:
711	        raise ValueError("archive items must be a non-empty tuple")
712	    if item_count > 0xFFFFFFFF:
713	        raise ValueError("too many HPB archive items")
714	    signer_count = _check_history_proof_bundle_signature(archive.signature)
715	    if signer_count > 0xFFFFFFFF:
716	        raise ValueError("too many signer ids")
717	
718	    # Encode every item first — each call raises TypeError/ValueError
719	    # for an illegal bundle exactly as the single-bundle codec does —
720	    # and only then frame the results, so a single illegal item aborts
721	    # the whole archive.
722	    frames = []
723	    for index, item in enumerate(items):
724	        encoded = encode_hpb(item)
725	        if len(encoded) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
726	            raise ValueError(
727	                f"HPB archive item {index + 1} encoding too long"
728	            )
729	        frames.append(encoded)
730	
731	    buffer = bytearray(HPBA_WIRE_TAG)
732	    buffer += item_count.to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
733	    for encoded in frames:
734	        buffer += len(encoded).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
735	        buffer += encoded
736	    buffer += _encode_varint(archive.signature.R)
737	    buffer += _encode_varint(archive.signature.z)
738	    buffer += signer_count.to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
739	    for signer_id in archive.signature.signer_ids:
740	        buffer += _encode_varint(signer_id)
741	    return bytes(buffer)
742	
743	
744	def decode_hpba(blob: bytes) -> HPBArchive:
745	    """Decode the canonical encoding produced by :func:`encode_hpba`.
746	
747	    Accepts only the single canonical form: the tag
748	    ``b"ts/hpba/w1"``, a 4-byte unsigned big-endian non-zero item
749	    count ``n``, then exactly ``n`` frames, each a 4-byte unsigned
750	    big-endian non-zero byte length followed by the exact canonical
751	    encoding of one :class:`HPB` that :func:`decode_hpb` accepts,
752	    and finally the outer signature frame: the length-prefixed integers
753	    ``R`` and ``z`` with ``R`` positive, the 4-byte non-zero signer
754	    count ``k`` and then exactly ``k`` strictly increasing positive
755	    signer ids. The bundles are restored in their original order as a
756	    tuple; they are neither sorted nor matched against one another or
757	    against the outer signature, and no signature is verified —
758	    :func:`verify_hpba` judges the archive afterwards. A non-bytes
759	    argument raises TypeError; a wrong or missing tag, a zero item
760	    count, a zero or over-long frame length, a declared count that does
761	    not match the number of frames, a nested bundle encoding that is
762	    illegal or non-canonical (including a frame that would not
763	    re-encode byte for byte), a zero ``R``, a non-canonical integer
764	    (leading zero or over-long length), a zero signer count, a
765	    non-positive or non-increasing signer id, truncation, or trailing
766	    bytes raises ValueError. A successfully decoded archive re-encodes
767	    to exactly the input bytes.
768	
769	    Decoding only restores structure: every nested bundle is decoded
770	    with :func:`decode_hpb` (which verifies no proof and checks no
771	    signature) and the outer signature is not checked. A structurally
772	    legal archive whose bundles do not verify or whose outer signature
773	    does not sign the bundles is returned normally, and
774	    :func:`verify_hpba` reports it as ``False``.
775	    """
776	    if not isinstance(blob, bytes):
777	        raise TypeError("blob must be bytes")
778	    if not blob.startswith(HPBA_WIRE_TAG):
779	        raise ValueError("bad HPB archive tag")
780	    offset = len(HPBA_WIRE_TAG)
781	
782	    if offset + 4 > len(blob):
783	        raise ValueError("truncated HPB archive item count")
784	    item_count = int.from_bytes(blob[offset:offset + 4], "big")
785	    offset += 4
786	    if item_count == 0:
787	        raise ValueError("HPB archive items must be non-empty")
788	
789	    items = []
790	    for index in range(item_count):
791	        frame, offset = _read_archive_block(
792	            blob,
793	            offset,
794	            what=f"HPB archive item {index + 1}",
795	        )
796	        items.append(decode_hpb(frame))
797	
798	    signature, offset = _read_bundle_signature_frame(
799	        blob, offset, what="HPB archive"
800	    )
801	    if offset != len(blob):
802	        raise ValueError("trailing bytes after HPB archive")
803	
804	    archive = HPBArchive(items=tuple(items), signature=signature)
805	    if encode_hpba(archive) != blob:
806	        raise ValueError("non-canonical HPB archive encoding")
807	    return archive

811	# Cross-key append-only proofs: a seal-history consistency statement whose
812	# old and new root signatures come from different threshold keys, linked by a
813	# non-empty RotationChain proving the path from the old key to the new one.
814	# The extension body E carries only the fixed-width tree statement
815	# ``U64(old_total) || U64(n) || leaves`` and C is the existing canonical
816	# rotation-chain encoding; both root signatures are the existing canonical
817	# bundle signature frames. The value is frozen and keeps no state —
818	# verify_rotation_chain authorizes the key path and the two root checks
819	# certify the prefix relation under each endpoint's own group parameters.
820	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
821	
822	RHE_WIRE_TAG = b"ts/rhe/v1"
823	
824	
825	@dataclass(frozen=True)
826	class RHE:
827	    """A cross-key seal-history append proof.
828	
829	    The fields, in order, are ``extension`` (a :class:`SealHistoryExtension`
830	    carrying the full new history's leaf digests), ``rotations`` (a
831	    non-empty, order-preserving :class:`RotationChain` from the old signing
832	    key to the new one), ``old_sig`` (the old key's
833	    :class:`AggregateSignature` on the old
834	    ``b"sh/r" || U64(old_total) || old_root`` statement) and ``new_sig``
835	    (the new key's :class:`AggregateSignature` on the new
836	    ``b"sh/r" || U64(n) || new_root`` statement). The dataclass is frozen,
837	    positionally constructible and compared by value, has no field
838	    defaults, and carries no network, storage or hidden state. Field types
839	    and bounds are not checked at construction time —
840	    :func:`encode_rhe` checks the structure and :func:`check_rhe` is the
841	    way to test a proof afterwards.
842	    """
843	
844	    extension: SealHistoryExtension
845	    rotations: RotationChain
846	    old_sig: AggregateSignature
847	    new_sig: AggregateSignature
848	
849	
850	def _rhe_extension_body(
851	    old_total: int, leaves: tuple[bytes, ...]
852	) -> bytes:
853	    """The fixed-width extension body ``E = U64(old_total) || U64(n) || leaves``."""
854	    buffer = bytearray(_history_proof_u64(old_total))
855	    buffer += _history_proof_u64(len(leaves))
856	    for leaf in leaves:
857	        buffer += leaf
858	    return bytes(buffer)
859	
860	
861	def _check_rhe_fields(
862	    x: object,
863	) -> tuple[
864	    SealHistoryExtension,
865	    RotationChain,
866	    AggregateSignature,
867	    AggregateSignature,
868	    int,
869	    tuple[bytes, ...],
870	]:
871	    """Type- and structure-check an :class:`RHE`, returning its parts.
872	
873	    The extension goes through the same structural checks as
874	    :func:`check_history_extension`, the chain through those of
875	    :func:`verify_rotation_chain` (without verifying any certificate), and
876	    both signatures through the bundle signature structure checks. Nothing
877	    here verifies a signature or a linkage.
878	    """
879	    if not isinstance(x, RHE):
880	        raise TypeError("x must be an RHE instance")
881	    old_total, leaves = _validate_history_extension_structure(x.extension)
882	    if not isinstance(x.rotations, RotationChain):
883	        raise TypeError("x.rotations must be a RotationChain instance")
884	    _check_rotation_chain_fields(x.rotations.anchor, x.rotations.certificates)
885	    _check_history_proof_bundle_signature(x.old_sig, field="x.old_sig")
886	    _check_history_proof_bundle_signature(x.new_sig, field="x.new_sig")
887	    return x.extension, x.rotations, x.old_sig, x.new_sig, old_total, leaves
888	
889	
890	def encode_rhe(x: RHE) -> bytes:
891	    """Canonically encode a cross-key append proof for transport or persistence.
892	
893	    The encoding is, in order, the tag ``b"ts/rhe/v1"``, the 4-byte unsigned
894	    big-endian length ``len(E)`` followed by the fixed-width extension body
895	    ``E = U64(old_total) || U64(n) || leaf_1 || ... || leaf_n`` where both
896	    counts are 8-byte unsigned big-endian and the leaves are the extension's
897	    32-byte digests in order, the 4-byte unsigned big-endian length
898	    ``len(C)`` followed by ``C = encode_rotation_chain(x.rotations)``, and
899	    then the old and new signature frames, each exactly the canonical
900	    signature frame of :func:`encode_history_proof_bundle`:
901	    ``VARINT(R)``, ``VARINT(z)``, the 4-byte unsigned big-endian signer
902	    count and one ``VARINT(id)`` per ascending signer id.
903	
904	    Only structure is checked: the extension and chain must be well formed
905	    (the exact bounds of :func:`check_history_extension` and
906	    :func:`encode_rotation_chain`) and both signatures structurally legal,
907	    but the rotation chain is not verified, neither signature is checked
908	    against a root and the two signatures may belong to unrelated groups —
909	    :func:`check_rhe` stays the way to verify a proof afterwards. Wrong
910	    argument or field types raise TypeError; an empty rotation chain, an
911	    empty or mis-sized leaf set, an out-of-range ``old_total``, a leaf that
912	    is not exactly 32 bytes, a negative chain anchor, an illegal chain
913	    certificate, an illegal signature, or an over-long frame raises
914	    ValueError. The output for a given proof is unique and the encoding
915	    carries no network, storage or hidden state.
916	    """
917	    extension, rotations, old_sig, new_sig, old_total, leaves = (
918	        _check_rhe_fields(x)
919	    )
920	
921	    extension_body = _rhe_extension_body(old_total, leaves)
922	    chain_body = encode_rotation_chain(rotations)
923	    old_signer_count = _check_history_proof_bundle_signature(
924	        old_sig, field="x.old_sig"
925	    )
926	    new_signer_count = _check_history_proof_bundle_signature(
927	        new_sig, field="x.new_sig"
928	    )
929	    if len(extension_body) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
930	        raise ValueError("rhe extension encoding too long")
931	    if len(chain_body) > 0xFFFFFFFF:
932	        raise ValueError("rhe rotation chain encoding too long")
933	    if old_signer_count > 0xFFFFFFFF or new_signer_count > 0xFFFFFFFF:
934	        raise ValueError("too many signer ids")
935	
936	    buffer = bytearray(RHE_WIRE_TAG)
937	    buffer += len(extension_body).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
938	    buffer += extension_body
939	    buffer += len(chain_body).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
940	    buffer += chain_body
941	    for signature in (old_sig, new_sig):
942	        buffer += _encode_varint(signature.R)
943	        buffer += _encode_varint(signature.z)
944	        buffer += len(signature.signer_ids).to_bytes(4, "big", signed=False)
945	        for signer_id in signature.signer_ids:
946	            buffer += _encode_varint(signer_id)
947	    return bytes(buffer)

950	def decode_rhe(b: bytes) -> RHE:
